title: Is the fringe part of the green?
question: If your ball comes to rest on the fringe just beside the green, is it treated as being on the putting green according to the rules?

choices.text: Yes, the fringe is part of the green
No, only the green itself counts
Only if any part of your ball touches the green and the fringe at the same time
It depends where your feet are standing

explanation: According to the rules, the fringe is not part of the putting green, even if it is right next to it. Only the area marked as the putting green counts.

juniorVersion.title: Is the grass around the green part of the green?
juniorVersion.question: If your ball stops on the short grass right next to the green, is that counted as being on the putting green in golf?

choices.text: Yes, the grass next to the green counts as the green
No, only the putting green itself counts
Only if part of your ball sits on both the green and the grass
It matters where you stand with your feet

juniorVersion.explanation: The short grass next to the green is called the 'fringe.' The rules say only the putting green counts as the green, not the fringe, even if it’s very close.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short grass right next to the putting green, but not part of the green.
The smooth, flat area where you try to putt the ball in the hole.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Draw a picture showing the putting green and the fringe to help kids see the difference.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids might think the fringe is the same as the green because it is so close.
Kids may think where their feet are changes the rule.
